title: The Story of the Atom
summary: From Kanad's paramanu to Dalton's solid spheres, Thomson's plum pudding, Rutherford's nucleus and Bohr's shells: how evidence changed our model of the atom.

ib.note: Excellent context for the nature of science: models change with evidence

cbse.chapter: Ch 3: Atoms and Molecules (Dalton's atomic theory); Ch 4: Structure of the Atom (Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr)

objectives: I can describe how the model of the atom developed: Kanad, Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr.
I can explain what Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed and why it changed the model.
I can explain why scientific models change when new evidence appears.
misconceptions: Atoms are solid little balls with nothing inside.
Scientists always knew what atoms look like.
An old model being replaced means those scientists were bad at science.
